row.short_description: Southern Italy & Sicily, Featuring Taormina, Matera and the Amalfi Coast, Palermo, Monreale, Agrigento’s Valley of the Temples, Piazza Amerina, Giardini Naxos, Strait of Messina, Sorrento, Positano, Pompeii, and more
row.full_description:
HH SOCIAL SOUTHERN ITALY & SICILY is a hosted group trip through a crossroads of civilizations in Sicily and on to the spectacular coastlines of Southern Italy. The trip was planned around 14 days, a classic travel style, and an age old heritage of ancient monuments and cultivated lands. The route includes Palermo, Monreale, the Valley of the Temples at Agrigento, Piazza Armerina, Giardini Naxos, Taormina, the Strait of Messina, Matera, Sorrento, Positano, and Pompeii. Along the way the journey lets the unique culture capture your heart.

Sicily is a place where history layers upon history. Palermo sits on the northern coast, a city with a thousand years of history, beautiful Arab Norman architecture, amazing food, and lively neighbourhoods. Nearby Monreale is known for its cathedral. Just outside Agrigento lies the Valley of the Temples, one of the most important archaeological sites in Sicily, with remarkably well preserved Doric temples and sweeping views of the countryside. Giardini Naxos lies on the east coast, with the mountain town of Taormina just above it. In Taormina you can stand in awe before the ancient Greek theatre. The Strait of Messina is reached through the port in the northeast corner of Sicily.

Crossing to the mainland, the trip was planned around time in Matera, capital of the Matera province in Basilicata, famous for its sassi, well preserved rock cut settlements that form a World Heritage site. The spectacular Amalfi Coast follows, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its iconic medieval cliffside fishing villages. Positano is a small picturesque town perched on the face of a hill, winding down towards the water, called the pearl of the Amalfi Coast. Sorrento overlooks the Bay of Naples and is widely known for its ceramics, lacework, and woodwork shops. The route also includes Pompeii, the ruined ancient Roman city considered one of the few sites where an ancient city has been preserved in detail.

Along the way you can experience true Sicilian hospitality during a farmhouse lunch, and enjoy a winery tour and tasting. The planned pace is Level 3 Active. You should be comfortable walking and standing for longer periods of time, and a moderately paced walking tour over hills and uneven surfaces should be no problem. Expect some longer days balanced with free time to recharge or set out on your own adventure. This level is not a fit for travellers who require mobility assistance devices.

Whether you dream of ancient temples, hilltop towns, or cliffside coastal villages, there is plenty to explore. row.full_description:
The CROATIA COASTLINE YACHT CRUISE is a twelve day journey along the Adriatic by yacht, taking in walled towns, islands and the Croatian capital. The route includes Dubrovnik, Slano, Korčula, Vis, Biševo, Hvar, Stari Grad, Boi, Split, Trogir, Sibenik, Vodice and Zagreb. Along the way you can wander historic centres, sail past brilliant blue water and explore stone streets shaped by centuries of history.

Dubrovnik is a historic walled city on the Adriatic coast in the far south of Croatia. It is nicknamed the Pearl of the Adriatic and is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. You can stroll the City Walls, pause at Big Onofrio's Fountain and visit the Rector's Palace.

Slano is a village in southern Croatia with a small harbour in the bay of the same name, a quiet stop along the coast. Korčula is a Croatian island in the Adriatic Sea, known for Grk, a white wine produced only on the island and not exported due to limited production. Biševo is a Croatian island in the Adriatic Sea.

Hvar reveals one of the largest squares in Dalmatia. Imposing fortifications hover above a blend of grey stone and orange roofs, and marble streets lead to the prized Cathedral of St. Stephen and the Renaissance theatre. Stari Grad shares this stretch of coast, with its quaint fishing harbour and wide promenade edging the sea.

Split is a city in Central Dalmatia, built around the Diocletian palace, where locals once sought refuge. Wandering the historic centre you can still see Roman walls, squares and temples. Trogir is a medieval town near Split, popular as a day trip because it sits within the metropolitan area. Sibenik and Vodice offer old streets, churches and quiet corners to explore.

Zagreb is the capital of Croatia, a city in Central Croatia with a charming medieval old city. Its architecture and cobbled streets are reminiscent of Vienna, Budapest, Prague and other Central European capitals.

This trip blends time on the water with time ashore, so you can relax on deck and then step into a different town each time you dock. The mix of islands, walled cities and the capital gives you both coastal calm and lively culture. Croatia rewards slow wandering, good wine and views of the Adriatic.

If this sounds like your kind of holiday, a travel specialist can help you plan this. Ask about this trip and share what you are hoping for, and we can help you plan the details together.

Related: [Croatia](/destinations/croatia).

row.full_description:
The SANDY TOES & SALTY SOULS GIRLS TRIP was planned around a lovely, sun-filled 4 nights adventure in Montego Bay, Jamaica. The stay was planned at the Iberostar Waves Rose Hall Beach Resort. This is a trip designed for friends who want warm days, soft sand and easy time together by the sea.

Montego Bay, commonly referred to as MoBay, is the second largest city in the island nation Jamaica. It is a popular spring break destination, so it suits a group looking for sunshine and a relaxed island mood. The area offers a lovely mix of beaches, culture and gentle adventure, all close enough to enjoy on a short getaway.

Along the way you can picture bright beach days. Doctor's Cave Beach, Cornwall Beach and Walter Fletcher Beach are all part of the Montego Bay scene. For a little history, Rose Hall Great House gives a glimpse into the island's past. The Centerstage Theatre adds an option for an evening out. Nature lovers may enjoy the Rockland Bird Sanctuary, a calm spot to watch the local birds.

For those who want more activity, Montego Bay has plenty to explore. Dunn’s River Falls & Park is a classic Jamaican outing. Chukka Caribbean Adventures and the John Halls Montego Bay Adventure Tour offer ways to see more of the island. Water fans might consider KiteBoarding Jamaica or the Montego Bay Sea Trek Adventure. Golf is another option for a slower afternoon. Getting around is simple with Jamaican Taxi Tours.

The Iberostar Waves Rose Hall Beach Resort sits in this same part of Montego Bay, so the beach and the local sights are all within reach. It makes a comfortable home base for a girls trip, where the days can be as busy or as restful as your group likes. You can swim, soak up the sun, and gather in the evenings to share the day.

This is a warm, friendly kind of trip, built for laughter and easy conversation. It works well for a group of friends who want time away together without a long or complicated itinerary. Four nights is enough to unwind, feel the salt air and come home refreshed.
